entities.name: Feng Yi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Feng Yi (died 34 CE) was a pivotal military general whose strategic acumen and battlefield prowess were instrumental in the establishment and early stabilization of the Eastern Han dynasty across a fragmented China. Operating within the tumultuous transitional period following the collapse of Wang Mang's Xin dynasty, Feng Yi emerged as a trusted confidant and leading commander under Emperor Guangwu of Han. His contributions were critical in unifying the empire and securing its nascent borders, particularly in the central plains and western regions, thus helping to lay the foundation for four centuries of renewed imperial stability.

His military career was defined by a series of decisive campaigns against regional warlords and, most notably, the formidable Red Eyebrows rebels. In 26 CE, Feng Yi achieved a significant victory against the Red Eyebrows at Heshui, demonstrating his tactical skill by encircling and routing a much larger force, capturing thousands of rebels and disrupting their supply lines. Later, in 27 CE, he played a crucial role in the final defeat of the Red Eyebrows near Chang'an, effectively dismantling the most widespread and destructive peasant uprising of the era and securing the former imperial capital.

Feng Yi's disciplined leadership and unwavering loyalty were exemplary. He was one of the "Twenty-Eight Generals of Yuntai," posthumously honored for their foundational contributions to the Eastern Han. His successes not only consolidated Emperor Guangwu's authority but also helped re-establish a centralized, effective administration after decades of chaos. His campaigns significantly reduced the internal threats that plagued the early Eastern Han, allowing for economic recovery and social reconstruction.
